title: E212: Update MCC list
description:
Op. Bulletin No. 1117 (1.II.2017) has an annexed list of Mobile
Country Codes that includes a number of which are not mentioned
in the MCC/MNC combined list in Op. Bulletin No. 1161 (1.XX.2018),
possibly because the MNCs are not reported to the ITU in a timely
fashion or because the assigned number is not actually used (e.g.,
Vatican City). See:
https://www.itu.int/dms_pub/itu-t/opb/sp/T-SP-OB.1117-2017-OAS-PDF-E.pdf

notes.body: So have you checked that those PLMNs were not removed in any intermediate amendment? It happened several time when I was going through the painful update of this list. Bulletin 1161 is supposed to be a full list of the valid PLMNs by that time. I'm not sure this is a right move, and it's gonna make our life real hard (it's already a pain to update this list).

I have checked that all those MCCs are still assigned. Almost all of them have PLMNs that are operational but have never appeared in a ITU operational bulletin for whatever reason.

I am fine with not adding PLMNs that we only have evidence for from non ITU sources, but the country code part is assigned and in an official document. I would like to at least get the correct country displayed even if the MNC is listed unknown. It's inaccurate to claim that these are Unassigned.

I think that the MCC list should have the ITU officially assigned MCC list (which is in Bulletin 1117 plus any amendments), and the PLMN list(s) should have the ITU official MCC+MNC list (which is in Bulletin 1161 plus amendments.)

I don't think it makes life harder to do that, rather than updating the MCC list to "only MCCs that have PLMNs on the PLMN list." There are various national telecommunications regulatory bodies that do not sent the information to the ITU, but the ITU still has those MCCs assigned (and in reality those PLMNs exist.) If I have a capture from one of these networks, I'd strongly prefer that it correctly label the MCC, even if the PLMN is listed as Unknown, rather than saying "Unassigned" for the MCC as well.

Updating with information from 3rd party sources _does_ make our life more difficult (and looks like it has been done in some cases), but that's not what is being done here.

The best would be to have access to the GSMA list instead (which is much more up to date than the E.212 one from my past experience) but it reuires being a member of the GSM Association... That's a shame.
